It is written for the Operations payments and wire room staff, Technology SRE on-call, and Compliance partners who need to understand how payments flow through the firm. No client names, account numbers, or routing details belong in tickets, Slack, or this document. Refer to payments by internal payment reference only. No placeholders are used in this document because it contains no personal or account data.

Dependencies
PaymentsGateway depends on GLCore (general ledger) for posting and balance checks, and on FraudScore (Compliance-owned) for real-time transaction scoring. FraudScore itself depends on DataLake. WireRoom, the wire transfer operations console, sits downstream of PaymentsGateway and cannot release wires if the gateway is unavailable. SettlementEngine does not call PaymentsGateway directly, but both rely on GLCore, so a GLCore outage will affect settlement and payments at the same time.

Normal Operating Windows
ACH origination files are cut at the daily cutoff and transmitted by the payments specialists (Craig Garner, Ronald Lewis). Outgoing wires are released by the wire room (Greg King, Derrick Anderson, Mike Herrera) through WireRoom, with the Fedwire cutoff as the hard deadline. Any wire queued after the afternoon cutoff rolls to next business day and the requesting relationship manager must be told.

Daily Health Checks
Performed by the wire room lead each morning before the first release:
1. Confirm the PaymentsGateway status page shows all nodes healthy.
2. Confirm FraudScore is returning scores with latency under the agreed threshold. If scoring is stale, do not release wires; escalate to Compliance.
3. Confirm GLCore posting is current and the prior day's ACH batch is marked settled.
4. Check the WireRoom queue for items older than one business day and escalate each to the payments specialist on duty.
5. Post a short all-clear in #it-ops or flag the issue.

Common Failure Modes
FraudScore timeouts: The gateway fails closed. Payments above the review threshold are held with status PENDING_SCORE. Do not override. Page Compliance engineering (Jenna Cho) and open an incident in #incidents. Held items are released only after scoring returns or a Compliance analyst manually clears them.

GLCore posting lag: Payments accept but remain unposted. Check with the GL team in Operations before re-submitting. Never resubmit a payment without confirming it was not already posted, as this creates duplicates.

WireRoom console unavailable but gateway healthy: Wire room staff should contact SRE (Omar Brown or Barbara Beard). Manual release procedures are allowed only with dual approval from two wire room specialists and sign-off from Ravi Patel or Linda Brandt.

ACH file rejection: Review the return code, correct the batch, and retransmit before the cutoff if possible. Log every rejected batch in the daily ops log.

Incident Response
Severity 1: Gateway fully down or wires cannot be released before cutoff. Page SRE on-call and the Head of Operations immediately, open a thread in #incidents, and notify Compliance. Linda Brandt is informed as COO. Provide updates every 30 minutes.
Severity 2: Degraded performance, partial holds, or elevated fraud-score latency. Open a ticket, notify #it-ops, and monitor hourly.
Severity 3: Single-payment issue or cosmetic console problem. Handle through the normal ticket queue.

After any Sev 1 or Sev 2, the incident owner writes a short review within three business days covering timeline, root cause, customer impact, and follow-up actions.

Controls and Approvals
Wire releases above the dual-control limit require two separate approvers; the initiator can never be an approver. Changes to beneficiary instructions require callback verification through a known contact on file, performed by someone other than the requester. Any suspected fraud or sanctions concern is escalated immediately to Compliance (Nadia Petrov for AML matters) and the payment is held. Do not discuss the reason for a hold with the requester until Compliance gives clearance.

Change Management
Deployments to PaymentsGateway are owned by Technology and require Operations approval. No changes are made during the last two hours before the wire cutoff or during month-end close. Rollback plans must be attached to the change ticket.

Reconciliation
End-of-day payment totals are reconciled against GLCore by Tasha Greene. Breaks are posted in #recon with the internal payment reference and aging. Breaks older than two business days are escalated to Ravi Patel.

Contacts
Operations: Ravi Patel, payments specialists, wire room
Technology SRE: Omar Brown, Barbara Beard
Compliance engineering: Jenna Cho
AML: Nadia Petrov

This runbook is reviewed quarterly. Send corrections to Ravi Patel.
